introduction: On this Sunday, God tells Jeremiah that he knew him before he was formed in the womb and made him a prophet to the nations. In the Gospel, the people of Nazareth turn against Jesus and try to throw him from a cliff, but he passes through their midst. Paul gives us his great hymn to love: love is patient, love is kind. Let us ask for the gift of love that never fails.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, love never fails. Let us bring our prayers to the God of love.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be known above all by her love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For prophets and witnesses who are rejected: that God may make them strong and stand by them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For married couples, families and communities: that their love may be patient, kind and faithful. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whom no one loves: that they may meet the love of God through us. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may know that God formed us and called us before we were born. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of love, you knew us before we were formed in the womb. Fill us with your love, which is patient and kind, and make us faithful witnesses to your Son. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The greatest of these is love
reflection.body:
God's word to the young Jeremiah could be spoken to every human being: "Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. Before you were born, I sanctified you." Jeremiah is called to a hard mission, and God promises him strength: "They will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you; for I am with you."

In the Gospel, the people of Nazareth have just heard Jesus speak in their synagogue. At first they admire his "gracious words," but then they ask, "Isn't this Joseph's son?" Jesus reminds them that God's prophets were often sent to outsiders: Elijah to a widow in Sidon, Elisha to Naaman the Syrian. The crowd is furious and tries to throw him off a cliff. "But he, passing through the middle of them, went his way." From the start, Luke shows us that Jesus' mission will meet rejection, and that his love reaches beyond borders.

Paul's hymn to love is one of the most famous passages in the Bible, often read at weddings. But Paul wrote it to a divided community that was proud of its spiritual gifts. Without love, he says, all gifts are empty: "If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don't have love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal."

Then he describes love: "Love is patient and is kind. Love doesn't envy. Love doesn't brag, is not proud." It "bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things. Love never fails." And he concludes, "But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love."

This week, read Paul's hymn slowly, and put your own name in place of the word love. Where does it fit, and where does it not yet? Ask God for the love you are missing.
